papers.title: Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China
papers.authors: Wang Wen-quan, Ting Du, Jiangxia Ye, Xiaohong Huang, Yangyang Li
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species-specific contributions. We integrated the environmental niches of the pathogen, hosts, and vectors to characterize abiotic constraints and biotic influences on PWD risk, quantify species-specific contributions and interactions, and inform surveillance priorities. RESULTS: Ensemble ecological niche models were developed for PWN, 17 susceptible hosts, and 10 potential cerambycid vectors across China and integrated with GeoDetector analysis. Although suitability patterns were broadly consistent, PWN had a much narrower suitable range than hosts and vectors, and this concordance declined under future climate scenarios. Bioclimatic variables were the primary determinants of habitat suitability for most species, whereas PWN showed narrower optimal ranges for key environmental drivers than most hosts and vectors. papers.title: A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica)
papers.authors: Davide Martinetti, Laura Erbetta, Danièle Bevacqua, Olivier Bonnefon, Marino Gatto
papers.abstract: Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities. Here we develop a process-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short-distance human-mediated transport, and ovo-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023. papers.title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
papers.authors: Toni M. Withers, Andrew R. Pugh, Darryl A. Herron, Dean Satchell, Shaun Wilkinson
papers.source: OpenAlex / New Zealand Journal of Zoology
papers.abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. This sequence of events leading to finding an established population highlights the potential for citizen science observations and eDNA monitoring to both uncover and pinpoint a cryptic pest's location as part of biosecurity surveillance.

papers.title: Predicting plant invasions and range shifts in an era of climate change
papers.authors: Matthew E. Fertakos
papers.abstract: The combined effects of invasive species and climate change have disastrous consequences on ecosystems, economies, and human health across the globe. As one of the driving forces behind modern extinctions, invasive plants outcompete native species, cause erosion, alter nutrient composition in soils, increase the prevalence of wildfires, as well as host and transmit pests and parasites. Meanwhile, rapid climate change is outpacing the ability of some native plant species to shift their ranges through natural dispersal. My dissertation explores how and why plants become invasive, solutions we can implement to improve prevention and slow their spread, and how we can restore and conserve species already negatively impacted by invasions. One of the main introduction pathways for invasive plants is the ornamental plant trade. For centuries, non-native plants have been transported from overseas to be bought and sold outside of their native ranges, some of which have escaped cultivation, established in the natural landscape, and subsequently become invasive. papers.title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
papers.authors: Yuxin Qiao, Jianquan Liu, David P. Edwards
papers.abstract: Abstract Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

papers.title: Sensitivity evaluation and multi-omics analysis of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus populations to emamectin benzoate in Shandong province field
papers.authors: Kunyang Ju, Zhifan Ma, Shuhan Guo, YuKe Wang, Shengnan Dong
papers.abstract: Pine trees provide substantial ecological and economic benefits worldwide, including water conservation, timber production, and carbon sequestration. However, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , as the pathogen of pine wilt disease (PWD), results in extensive pine mortality annually, posing a serious threat to global pine resources and environmental security. Currently, chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing PWD. In Shandong Province, emamectin benzoate (EB) is the main nematicide for trunk injection. Nevertheless, long-term use of a single compound carries a high risk of resistance development. In this study, the sensitivity of 15 B. xylophilus strains from different regions of Shandong Province to EB was evaluated. The highest and lowest LC 50 values were observed in the PL (320.99 μg•mL -1 ) and CD strains (114.63 μg•mL -1 ), respectively, yielding a resistance ratio (PL vs CD) of 2.8 < 5, indicating that EB resistance may not have developed in the B. xylophilus populations in Shandong. papers.title: From Pest Control to Health Protection: A Health-Based Hierarchy of Control for Sustainable Agriculture
papers.authors: Vivien How, Nur Azalina Suzianti Feisal
papers.abstract: The widespread reliance on synthetic pesticides remains a defining feature of modern agriculture, particularly in tropical and export-oriented farming systems. While these chemicals have contributed to yield stability and pest suppression, their long-term consequences for farmer health, environmental integrity, and food system sustainability remain insufficiently integrated within existing agricultural decision frameworks. In Malaysia and similar middle-income agricultural economies, synthetic pesticide adoption rooted in colonial-era agrochemical trials and intensified through the expansion of herbicides such as glyphosate, has fostered structurally chemical-dependent farming practices. These practices disproportionately transfer occupational and environmental health risks to farmers and rural communities. Current approaches to pesticide management, including Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and regulatory risk assessment, provide important but fragmented solutions. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Using CLIMEX and MaxEnt models to simulate the influence of climate change on the global distribution of the ghost ant Tapinoma melanocephalum (Hymenoptera: Formicidae)
papers.authors: Muhammad Ramzan, Guiqing Liu, Ramzi Mansour, Owusu Fordjour Aidoo, Ahmed Mahmoud Ismail
papers.abstract: The ghost ant, Tapinoma melanocephalum (Fabricius), is a globally distributed invasive species whose potential response to climate change remains poorly quantified. We applied MaxEnt and CLIMEX as complementary modeling approaches to estimate its current and future global climatic suitability. Both models showed acceptable performance and produced projections broadly consistent with the known distribution of T. melanocephalum. MaxEnt predicted widespread low climatic suitability, with high-suitability areas concentrated mainly in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa, and the Americas. CLIMEX identified extensive climatic suitability across South America, sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and parts of Europe. Moderate climatic suitability also extended into several temperate regions. Future MaxEnt projections under SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5 indicated substantial redistribution of climatic suitability during the 2050s and 2070s. Suitability increased across several temperate and higher-latitude regions but declined in some tropical areas. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.title: A Hybrid ConvLSTM Transfer Learning Framework for Cross-regional Prediction of Arecanut Disease Intensity
papers.authors: Bharathi K, Ashwini B, Shrikanth Rao S K, Prathibha V H

papers.title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
papers.authors: Niamjit Das, Kevin Andrew
papers.abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. papers.authors: Jean‐Claude Grégoire, Hazan Alkan Akıncı, Medea Burjanadze, Hugh Evans, Nick Fielding
papers.abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. A very specific predator, Rhizophagus grandis (Coleoptera, Monotomidae), has followed its prey in its territorial expansion, with temporal and spatial lags due to long distance passive transportation of D. micans with trade, and to habitat fragmentation. When both species coexist, D. micans is very sparce and only occasionally kills trees, because the high capacity of R. grandis to locate prey even at very low densities enables it to control the pest. This very particular relationship has been exploited for biological control. Mass production and inoculative releases of R. grandis have been undertaken in four countries: Georgia since 1963, France (1978), Great Britain (1983) and Türkiye (1985). papers.title: Implications, Benefits, Challenges, and Future Perspective of GIS-Farming Machinery Integration in Precision Agriculture: A Review
papers.authors: M. I Usman
papers.source: OpenAlex / INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
papers.abstract: This review examines the integration of geographic information systems (GIS) with agricultural machinery in the context of precision agriculture. It discusses the implications of this integration and demonstrates how GIS technology improves and enhances data collection, analysis, and decision-making processes in agriculture. The benefits outlined include improved resource management, increased crop yields, and improved sustainability practices. However, the paper also addresses the challenges of integrating GIS and agricultural machinery, such as high costs, technical complexity, and the need for qualified personnel. Finally, it outlines the prospects for the development of this integration. The potential of advances in technology and data analysis to further optimize agricultural practices is highlighted, focusing on the challenges, risks, and functional implications.

papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.authors: Farida B. Gabdrakhmanova, Ekaterina S. Churbanova, S. Е. Solovieva, Антипин Игорь Сергеевич
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. papers.abstract: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. papers.title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores
papers.authors: LiWen Kang, Junjie Chen, Mingsheng Hong, Wei Wei, Zuofu Xiang
papers.abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear. Here, we systematically analyzed OR repertoires across 25 carnivoran species occupying diverse niches. Marine carnivorans exhibit convergent OR degeneration, with fewer intact genes and ancestral orthologs, higher pseudogene ratios, and relaxed purifying selection compared with terrestrial species. Notably, bamboo-specialized giant pandas display identical degenerative signatures, possessing the smallest intact OR repertoire and most lost ancestral OR groups among terrestrial carnivorans. Our models show habitat primarily shapes intact OR quantity, while dietary specialization governs pseudogenization and selective constraints. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals.

papers.title: Sunflower sea star (Pycnopodia helianthoides) environmental DNA (eDNA) shedding and decay: Influence of sunlight and comparison to other marine organisms
papers.authors: Meghan M. Shea, Laura Kubiatko, Andrew Kim, Ashley Kidd, Zachary J. Gold
papers.abstract: Conservation practitioners increasingly turn to environmental DNA (eDNA) for biomonitoring, yet interpreting DNA-based data requires attention to organismal shedding and decay dynamics. Here, we characterize shedding rates and decay rate constants of eDNA from Pycnopodia helianthoides, a critically endangered and ecologically important sea star in the Northeast Pacific Ocean. Shedding rates were quantified via a mesocosm experiment utilizing twelve stars of varying sizes, and decay rate constants were calculated for naturally shed P. helianthoides eDNA under natural sunlit and dark conditions for 96 hours. We additionally completed a systematic search and review of marine organism shedding rates and decay rate constants. P. helianthoides decay rate constants (k) were not different under sunlit and dark conditions (average k=0.0257 hr-1) and among the lowest third reported for marine organisms. Similarly, biomass-normalized shedding rates (between 896 and 19,800 copies/hr/g) and shedding rates per individual (between 22,000 and 548,000 copies/hr/individual) were among the lowest recorded across marine organisms. papers.title: Sexual behavior dysfunction and sickness behavior as an early warning indicators of imidacloprid exposure, associated with pituitary–adrenal axis dysregulation and DNA damage in Japanese quails
papers.authors: Ramadan D. El Shoukary, Doaa S. Abd El-Maguid, Asmaa H. Abd El Kareem, Aymen S. Abd El-Maguid, Gehad Seddik
papers.abstract: Introduction Japanese quails ( Coturnix coturnix japonica ) serve as vital models in behavioral neuroendocrinology and ecotoxicology, particularly for understanding the neuroendocrine pathways regulating avian mating strategies. Subchronic exposure to neonicotinoid insecticides poses critical threats to avian reproduction and population dynamics. Methods This study comprehensively evaluated the neuroendocrine, behavioral, morphometric, and genotoxic impacts of chronic oral imidacloprid (IMI) exposure in Japanese quail ( Coturnix coturnix japonica ) across developmental and adult stages (weeks 7–12 of age). Results Imidacloprid administration significantly delayed pubertal onset and increased body weight at sexual maturity in both sexes ( p ≤ 0.003). papers.authors: Yun Xing, Fengxu Chen, Gonggeng Liu, Shijun Bao, Xujian Zhang
papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. However, large projects like the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Plant (HPP) in Pará, located in a sensitive Amazonian biome with numerous indigenous lands and traditional communities, have raised significant environmental and social concerns, often exacerbating social inequalities. papers.title: The coral settlement-sphere: microenvironments that shape reef restoration in the Anthropocene
papers.authors: Sarah Ling Romero, Peter L. Harrison, Alexandra Ordoñez Alvarez, Tom Shlesinger, Adi Khen
papers.abstract: Accelerating losses of reef-building corals are driving steep declines in coral recruitment, imperiling the biodiversity and long-term resilience of reef ecosystems worldwide. Here, we review the mechanisms underlying coral recruitment success through a critical – yet largely overlooked – microenvironmental lens relevant to the scale of microscopic coral larvae. We introduce the concept of the “settlement-sphere”, which encompasses the physical, biochemical, and microbial microhabitat properties that govern successful coral larval recruitment. We then examine how anthropogenic stressors erode this settlement-sphere by diminishing essential chemical cues, reducing microhabitat complexity, and altering key physico-chemical conditions (e.g., hypoxia), ultimately leading to recruitment failure. Finally, we argue that advancing a collective understanding of the settlement-sphere is essential for developing actionable strategies to restore degraded coral reef systems. papers.abstract: Non-native species are recognized as one of the major drivers of biodiversity change globally, with profound impacts on ecosystem functions and services. Despite the high number of studies on non-native species published, mainly in the last two decades, an often-overlooked aspect is their role as mediators of resource subsidies (the cross-boundary movement of energy, nutrients, or materials). This topic may have theoretical and empirical implications because non-native species may play a major role in ecosystem connectivity by transporting—or interrupting the transport of—energy and organic matter. Therefore, the main aims of this review were to (1) assess temporal trends, geographic distribution, and methodological approaches in research on resource subsidies mediated by non-native species; (2) synthesize how non-native species alter the magnitude, direction, and dynamics of resource subsidies across ecosystems and their implications for ecosystem functioning; and (3) identify key gaps in current knowledge and define future research priorities.
